posts.title: The Mysterious Speaking Machine of G. T. J. Müller
posts.description: In 1788, Georg Theodor Jacob Müller exhibited a “speaking machine” in Erlangen, Nuremberg, and Bayreuth. One of its features was an “echo”: audience members would privately speak three or four words into it, and then—after a brief delay—it would echo their speech back to them. posts.title: The Seventeenth-Century Speaking Automata of Paul Liégeois
posts.description: We don’t really know who built the first true speaking automaton—that is, a machine that could talk automatically, entirely by itself, once set in motion.
